# Governance and Secure Development Lifecycle (GOV)

How security is built into the way we plan, design and run development work.

## SCS-GOV-01 Treat security as a functional requirement

Level: MUST

Applies to: All (Flutter and Backend)

Policy: Every new application, feature or integration MUST have written security requirements, taken from this standard and the data classification, before development starts. They are tracked and tested alongside the functional, usability and performance requirements. Application security requirements MUST be reviewed and approved by the IT Security team.

Implementation (all stacks):

- Add a "Security requirements" section to the requirements for each application or feature, kept in its Git repository (for example docs/security-requirements.md): data classification, who may use it (roles), applicable SCS policy IDs, and any compliance needs (for example PDPL).
- Write acceptance criteria for the security requirements so they can be tested (see SCS-TEST-01).
- Use OWASP ASVS 5.0 as the checklist for web and API requirements, and OWASP MASVS v2 for mobile requirements.

Verification: Section Head confirms the feature has security requirements and IT Security approval before development starts.

## SCS-GOV-02 Assess risk and threat model new applications and major changes

Level: MUST

Applies to: All (Flutter and Backend)

Policy: Every new application, new external integration and major change MUST have a documented risk assessment and threat model before coding begins. It identifies data flows, trust boundaries, threats and the controls chosen, and sets the application's risk level. High-risk applications get extra scrutiny (penetration test, deeper review). The assessment MUST be repeated after major updates or a change in the threat landscape.

Implementation (all stacks):

- Draw a simple data flow diagram: users, apps, APIs, databases, SAP, third parties, and the trust boundaries between them.
- Use STRIDE (Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information disclosure, Denial of service, Elevation of privilege) per data flow, or the OWASP Threat Modeling Cheat Sheet.
- Classify the application as Low, Medium or High risk based on data sensitivity and exposure (internet-facing, personal data, financial data, SAP write access).
- Store the threat model in the repository (docs/threat-model.md) and update it when the design changes.

Verification: Threat model exists in the repository and is linked from the feature's requirements.

## SCS-GOV-03 Review the security architecture before building

Level: MUST

Applies to: All (Flutter and Backend)

Policy: New applications, major features and external integrations MUST have a security architecture review by the Security Reviewer before coding begins. The Section Head reviews the same design for technical fit. Designs MUST use approved frameworks and the organization's identity provider rather than custom security mechanisms.

Implementation (all stacks):

- The review checks the threat model, authentication and authorization design, data protection, secrets, logging and third-party components against this standard.
- Approved frameworks: Flutter stable channel and the packages vetted under SCS-SUP-01; ASP.NET Core LTS, EF Core, ASP.NET Core Identity / JWT Bearer, Azure Key Vault.
- Record the decision and any accepted risks in the repository (for example docs/architecture-review.md).

Verification: Architecture review sign-off is recorded in the repository before the first merge request of the feature.

## SCS-GOV-04 Protect development workstations and confidential designs

Level: MUST

Applies to: All (Flutter and Backend)

Policy: Developer workstations MUST have full-disk encryption, a screen lock and current patches. Developers MUST lock their screen when they leave it, and MUST NOT leave architecture diagrams, credentials or sensitive designs where visitors can see them.

Implementation (all stacks):

- BitLocker on Windows or FileVault on macOS; screen lock after at most 10 minutes of inactivity; Windows+L when you leave your desk.
- Do not keep production data, keys or signing keystores on laptops (see SCS-SEC-01).
- Wipe whiteboards with system designs after meetings in shared rooms.

Verification: IT endpoint management reports encryption status. Spot checks of desks and meeting rooms.

## SCS-GOV-05 Keep this standard current and acknowledged

Level: MUST

Applies to: All (Flutter and Backend)

Policy: This standard MUST be reviewed every six months and after major changes in the technology stack, team, regulation or threat landscape, or after an application security incident. Every team member MUST acknowledge each new version in writing. The document owner, Youssef Mahmoud, maintains this standard and approves changes to it.

Implementation (all stacks):

- Any team member proposes updates (new framework versions, new CVEs, lessons from incidents) to the document owner, as a merge request to the policy source files.
- Regenerate the three editions after every change (see CONFIGURATION.md) and record the version in the change history.

Verification: Change history shows a review within the last six months; signed acknowledgements are on file.
